bug_semantics: Commit.count accepted arbitrary keyword options and passed them unchanged to git rev-list without checking GitPython's unsafe revision options. If an application forwards attacker-controlled options, output=<path> becomes --output=<path>; git rev-list opens and truncates that path to zero bytes before Commit.count parses revision output, allowing file destruction at the application's privilege level.
flaw_origin: Commit.count originally exposed no option forwarding. Commit 806450db9b2c4a829558557ac90bd7596a0654e0 changed the class method in lib/git/objects/commit.py from def count(cls, repo, rev, paths='') to def count(cls, repo, rev, paths='', **kwargs) and changed the sink to repo.git.rev_list(rev, '--', paths, **kwargs), creating the unguarded caller-controlled option channel. Commit 0b3ecf2dcace76b65765ddf1901504b0b4861b08 later converted count to an instance method and substituted self.repo/self.id, but merely carried the already-vulnerable forwarding mechanism forward.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author and committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com> and contains only the message 'repo.commit_delta_base: removed'; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker.
evidence: The first-party advisory https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/security/advisories/GHSA-p538-c434-8v24 identifies the unguarded Commit.count rev-list kwargs sink, demonstrates count(output='/victim') truncating a file while the sibling iterator rejects the option, and declares package versions <=3.1.55 affected and >=3.1.56 patched. Its embedded description retains an older '<= 3.1.53' statement, but repository-tag source inspection below confirms that 3.1.54 and 3.1.55 are also vulnerable. The public alias is https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h75v-4jxv-ppxm.

History searches in the full clone, including git log -L over Commit.count and git log --follow -S "rev_list(rev, '--', paths, **kwargs)" -- lib/git/objects/commit.py, identify 806450db9b2c4a829558557ac90bd7596a0654e0 as the first commit adding both **kwargs to count and **kwargs to its rev_list call. The BIC diff and old-path source are first-party at https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/commit/806450db9b2c4a829558557ac90bd7596a0654e0 and https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/blob/806450db9b2c4a829558557ac90bd7596a0654e0/lib/git/objects/commit.py#L105-L124.

Direct-parent tree verification with git grep against 39229db70e71a6be275dafb3dd9468930e40ae48 found lib/git/objects/commit.py:127 as def count(cls, repo, rev, paths='') and line 144 as repo.git.rev_list(rev, '--', paths), with no forwarded **kwargs. The same tree query against 806450db9b2c4a829558557ac90bd7596a0654e0 found line 105 accepting **kwargs and line 124 forwarding **kwargs. Thus the vulnerable option channel is absent in the immediate parent, whose source is https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/blob/39229db70e71a6be275dafb3dd9468930e40ae48/lib/git/objects/commit.py#L127-L144.

The BIC is a normal one-parent commit (parent 39229db70e71a6be275dafb3dd9468930e40ae48), not a merge, revert, move, or identifiable squash. The later 0b3ecf2dcace76b65765ddf1901504b0b4861b08 instance-method conversion preserves the kwargs sink and is therefore not the BIC; no member-commit decomposition is applicable.

Commit 701ce32fe5ba8cb622c0e0342a376a6beb47d738 added unsafe_git_rev_options = ['--output', '-o'] and Git.check_unsafe_options to Commit.iter_items on 2026-07-12 but left Commit.count unchanged. The direct fix 38553b6fddc7f6a667cdb45a6762343a08fc72b2 adds allow_unsafe_options=False and invokes Git.check_unsafe_options on count's kwargs before either rev_list call, plus a regression check expecting UnsafeOptionError. First-party fix: https://github.com/gitpython-developers/GitPython/commit/38553b6fddc7f6a667cdb45a6762343a08fc72b2.

Tag containment shows the BIC first appears in tag 0.2.0-beta1 (tag commit 1019d4cf68d1acdbb4d6c1abb7e71ac9c0f581af); no 0.1.x tag contains it. At the upper boundary, git grep of tag 3.1.55 (commit 681c82c9c296f934635c81fa8294d4b6b6791b7e) shows count accepting and forwarding **kwargs without a local check, while tag 3.1.56 (commit e3221f1252346259513e14afeed32f0a203512a7) shows the new check at git/objects/commit.py:296. git for-each-ref --contains the fix reports 3.1.56 and later, not 3.1.55, matching the advisory's patched boundary.

BIC-only attribution used numactl-bound git cat-file commit 806450db9b2c4a829558557ac90bd7596a0654e0. The exact object has tree 3ddde84e1e94bc2bfb242e3dcc4f74d7ede5b8d5, parent 39229db70e71a6be275dafb3dd9468930e40ae48, author and committer Sebastian Thiel <byronimo@gmail.com>, and the single-line message 'repo.commit_delta_base: removed', with no trailers or AI/bot marker.
reasoning: The causal defect is not the later lack of a newly introduced helper by itself; it is the API-to-command channel that lets count callers inject arbitrary rev-list options. Commit 806450db9b2c4a829558557ac90bd7596a0654e0 is the smallest history unit that created that channel by adding and forwarding **kwargs, and its direct parent proves the channel did not exist immediately before. Subsequent formatting and the 0b3ecf2dcace76b65765ddf1901504b0b4861b08 class-to-instance refactor retain rather than originate it. The 2026 unsafe-option work made the dangerous --output/-o set explicit but guarded only the sibling iterator, leaving count exploitable until 38553b6fddc7f6a667cdb45a6762343a08fc72b2 applied the same check directly to count. Tag source and containment establish the historical lower bound and the 3.1.55/3.1.56 vulnerable-to-fixed transition. Because the exact BIC commit object is human-authored and human-committed with no commit-object AI signal, the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI; attribution on any later fix or refactor cannot change that result.
